requirements.requirement: On node1, record sudo command invocations in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with the invoking user and timestamp.
requirements.summary: The valid sudoers configuration directs sudo records to the required file and enables four-digit years. Direct probes show timestamped entries containing the invoking user “antrieb,” target user, and command, both before and after restart; the file is root-owned with mode 0600.

requirements.requirement: Keep the dedicated sudo command entries out of the general system log.
requirements.summary: The valid configuration disables sudo syslog output, and distinct pre- and post-restart command markers were absent from both /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure while present in the dedicated log.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied. Node1 records timestamped, user-attributed sudo commands in the required dedicated file and suppresses those command records from the general logs. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete and coherent: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the boot ID changed, and sudo configuration, prior data, new logging behavior, rsyslog, and normal system state recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Finite probes cannot literally exercise every possible future sudo command; completeness is supported by the global sudoers logfile setting plus multiple observed invocations.
Package-health collection timed out both before and after execution, so package consistency was not independently assessed; no executor command attempted package changes.
General-log exclusion was directly checked for /var/log/messages and /var/log/secure, the configured RHEL general and authpriv logs, rather than every possible log destination.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Temporary configuration files were created for necessary validation and removed within the same commands; installing /etc/sudoers.d/command_logging was the required implementation; probe-induced log writes were bounded final evidence; and the reboot served the mandatory provider restart protocol. After execution there were no failed services, no new listening interfaces, and no abandoned executor temporary files. Socket and systemd-private-directory differences reflect changed process IDs and boot identity after restart.
